spec.doc: Records `signer`'s vote for `outcome` (allowed only once `close_time` has passed). `Invalid` claims the question is unanswerable; an `Invalid` proposal finalizes by voiding the market. Split votes: every outcome, `Invalid` included, has its own counter, and a signer is deduplicated per `(outcome, signer)`, so one signer may attest several outcomes (existing behaviour, extended to `Invalid`). The first outcome to reach threshold becomes the proposal and later `Yes`/`No` quorums never move it. The one exception: `Invalid` reaching threshold replaces a pending `Yes`/`No` proposal and restarts the dispute window, because a quorum saying the question cannot be answered outranks an answer to it. An `Invalid` proposal is never replaced. (Requiring `Invalid` to beat every other count is a possible follow-up.)
spec.name: attest

spec.doc: Categorical counterpart of `attest`: `signer` attests that `outcome_index` is the winner. `outcome_index` must be below the `outcome_count` the market's commitment fixed. Once `threshold` members have attested an index it becomes the proposal and the dispute window opens.
spec.name: attest_cat

Only the proposal is removed: attestations and per-outcome counts stay, so the next attestation that brings any outcome to threshold (for example a further `Yes` once `Yes` already has quorum) proposes again. A categorical market keeps its pending winner in a separate slot, cleared the same way.
spec.name: cancel_proposal

spec.doc: Cancels a pending rotation for a committee (admin only).
spec.name: cancel_rotation

spec.doc: Pays a settled dispute's bond to its payee (the disputer, or the market-core treasury when the proposal was upheld). Permissionless.

The disputer escrows `dispute_bond` of the collateral token, which freezes finalization until the escalation authority rules or `escalation_timeout` lapses. `alternative` is the outcome the disputer claims is correct (`None`: the market is invalid); it only informs the ruling and must differ from the proposal (so `None` is rejected for an `Invalid` proposal). spec.name: propose_rotation

Only meaningful for markets whose `resolution_hash` commits to `ResolutionSpec::CategoricalSigners` with this exact `outcome_count`; the reveal target's `resolution_hash` is read from whichever market kind owns the id.

spec.doc: Reveals the resolution rule committed to at market creation. Anyone may call this (there is no admin gate) because the only thing that makes a spec acceptable is that it hashes to `market.resolution_hash` — the commitment, not the caller, is the authority. Fails if a spec was already registered for this market.
spec.name: register_price_spec

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, scalar mode: the market settles fractionally from the feed price clamped into `[lower, upper]` (see `resolve_scalar_price`).
spec.name: register_scalar_spec

spec.doc: Reveals a decimal-explicit price rule committed to as `sha256(SCALED_SPEC_DOMAIN || XDR(ScaledPriceConfig))` (issue #26). Same commit/reveal flow as [`register_price_spec`]; `threshold_decimals` above [`MAX_THRESHOLD_DECIMALS`] is `InvalidConfig` (no `i128` scale factor exists that large). The preimage is its own domain-tagged space rather than a `ResolutionSpec` variant because PR #176 moved that enum to `oracledesk-types` (edited only via maintainer follow-up; see ADR 0001) — every existing `Price` / `Signers` / V2 commitment stays byte-for-byte valid either way.
spec.name: register_scaled_price_spec

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, signer mode.
spec.name: register_signer_spec

spec.doc: Reveals a rule committed to through a [`ResolutionSpecV2`] envelope. The envelope must name this network and this resolver's market-core (`DomainMismatch`), use a non-zero salt and the current `version` (`InvalidConfig`), and hash to the market's commitment (`SpecHashMismatch`). The inner rule is then validated and stored exactly as the legacy entrypoints do.
spec.name: register_spec_v2

spec.doc: Reveals a time-weighted-average price rule committed to as `sha256(TWAP_SPEC_DOMAIN || XDR(TwapConfig))` (issue #27). Same commit/reveal flow as [`register_scaled_price_spec`], with two differences. First, the static validation ([`validate_twap_rule`]): `window > 0`, `min_samples >= 2`, `max_gap` in `(0, window]`, `threshold >= 0`. Second, feasibility is checked *against the live feed*: the grid period only exists on-chain, so registration calls `resolution()` on the configured reflector and rejects `window / resolution > MAX_TWAP_SAMPLES` or `min_samples > window / resolution` with `InvalidConfig`. This makes the reflector required reachable at registration (a trapping feed gives `PriceUnavailable`) — deliberate: an unresolvable TWAP market is caught at reveal time, not at close.
spec.name: register_twap_spec

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, weighted Ed25519 committee that signs off-chain and is verified by `submit_signatures`.
spec.name: register_weighted_key_spec

spec.name: resolution_deadline

spec.doc: #149: [`Resolver::resolve_price`] that pays the market's bounty to `caller`. The payout happens in the same invocation that makes the market final, so a call that fails also pays nothing.

spec.doc: Resolves a scalar market from its Reflector feed. The reading is clamped into the committed `[lower, upper]` range and settled as the fractional LONG payout `(clamped - lower) / (upper - lower)` in bps (SHORT pays the complement). Returns the payout. A non-positive reading is `InvalidPrice` rather than a clamp: it means the feed is broken, not that the value sits at the bottom of the range. Same close-time, staleness and terminal-state rules as `resolve_price`.
spec.name: resolve_scalar_price

spec.doc: Resolves a [`TwapConfig`] market (issue #27). Same lifecycle as `resolve_price` (closed, not terminal), and markets already revealed as TWAP also resolve through `resolve_price`, which dispatches here. Non-TWAP markets are `WrongMode`.

spec.doc: Pins the committed feed's price for `close_time` in resolver storage, so `resolve_price` still works after the oracle's bounded history has aged that record out (SEP-40 `price(asset, timestamp)` returns `None` outside the retained window). Permissionless: `caller` only authorizes being recorded as `taken_by`. Callable any time after `close_time` while the market is unresolved, but in practice it must run within the oracle's retention window (see `docs/architecture.md`, "Oracle history retention"). The first valid snapshot wins (`SnapshotExists` afterwards): for a fixed `(asset, close_time)` the answer is deterministic, and freezing it deliberately prefers determinism over an oracle later rewriting history. A price `resolve_price` would reject is never stored.
spec.name: snapshot_price

spec.doc: Which kind of rule `market_id` has revealed (`SpecKind::None` before any reveal). Existence checks only (`has`), so the read footprint stays minimal; a missing or archived entry reads as `None`, it never panics. Needed because `state()` stays `Unconfigured` for a revealed price or signer market (#273).

spec.doc: Pure view: no TTL extensions. The instance and the market's entries are kept alive by the mutating entrypoints above, so a view-only simulation stays read-only.

spec.doc: Counts Ed25519 signatures from a weighted committee. Permissionless: the signatures, not the submitter, carry the authority. Each signature is over the message built by `attestation_message`; non-members and keys that already signed this round (for either outcome) are skipped, and a single invalid signature aborts the whole batch, so submitters should pre-filter with a verifier. Once the accumulated weight for `outcome` first reaches the threshold a proposal is recorded and the dispute window starts; later calls never move it.
spec.name: submit_signatures

spec.doc: The spec kind, resolution state, deadline and proposal flag in one read: one cross-contract call from the treasury instead of four. Reads market-core's `close_time` once. A pure view: it does not extend any TTL (so a simulation stays read-only), unlike `instance_get`.

spec.doc: Scalar (range) counterpart of [`PriceConfig`]. The market settles on the fractional position of `price` inside `[lower, upper]`: `payout_long_bps = (clamped_price - lower) / (upper - lower)`, and the SHORT side pays the complement. A reading below the range clamps to `lower` (LONG pays 0), above to `upper` (LONG pays 1.0); a non-positive reading is an invalid price, never a clamp.

spec.doc: Decimal-explicit price rule (issue #26, goal 2). Unlike the legacy [`PriceConfig`] — re-exported here from `oracledesk-types`, whose `threshold` is in *feed-native units* and is compared to the raw feed price with no scaling, so every committed legacy hash and meaning is unchanged (ADR 0001) — this struct records `threshold_decimals`, and resolution rescales both the threshold and the feed price to `max(feed_decimals, threshold_decimals)` with checked arithmetic before comparing. A creator who means "$0.20" commits `threshold = 20`, `threshold_decimals = 2` instead of guessing the feed's scale. `PriceConfig` and `SignerConfig` deliberately do **not** appear here: PR #176 made `contracts/oracledesk-types` their canonical home and this crate re-exports them (see the `pub use` at the top of this file), so a `resolution_hash` commitment never depends on which crate declared the type. [`ScaledPriceConfig`] stays resolver-local for now for the same reason ADR 0001 can state its append-only rule so precisely
spec.name: ScaledPriceConfig

spec.doc: Time-weighted-average price rule (issue #27). The market settles on the average of the feed's records over a window ending at `close_time` instead of a single print: a manipulated or anomalous close record can no longer decide the market on its own. Like the legacy [`PriceConfig`] (and unlike [`ScaledPriceConfig`], issue #26) the `threshold` is in feed-native units — the TWAP is a raw-price average — and the committed comparison applies to the floored average (see `twap_outcome` and ADR 0001). `min_samples`/`max_gap` encode how much of the window the feed must actually have filled: resolution is rejected (`StalePrice`) below `min_samples` present records or when any gap — window start to first sample, consecutive samples, or last sample to `close_time` — exceeds `max_gap`. Same canonical-home note as [`ScaledPriceConfig`]: this is a resolver-local type committing through a domain-tagged preimage ([`twap_spec_hash`]) because PR #176 froze `oracledesk-types`' `ResolutionSpec` as the shared enum router
